subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should the remaining fix target the scheduled producer/prompt that asks for bad paths, or should OpenClaw change the generic read tool contract so directory reads list contents instead of failing?
rationale: Both shapes could reduce the observed errors, but the read-tool change is a model-facing behavior contract and the producer has not been located in current source.

options.title: Fix Producer First
options.body: Keep read semantics stable and repair the scheduler/prompt/source that generates memory-system/CORE.md and directory read requests after a live repro identifies it.

options.title: Change Read Contract
options.body: Make read list directories or redirect to ls, accepting a broader tool-contract change that needs tests and release-note context.

options.title: Hold For Live Repro
options.body: Keep the issue open until a current-build trace identifies whether the RSS growth comes from read errors, scheduled memory work, or another gateway retention path.

recommendation.title: Fix Producer First
recommendation.body: Keep read semantics stable and repair the scheduler/prompt/source that generates memory-system/CORE.md and directory read requests after a live repro identifies it.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice sits on the read-tool and heartbeat/scheduled-runtime boundary where this history has the strongest current routing signal.
